title: Computational and Memory Cost Profile (Pareto Trade-offs)
formal_question: What is the multi-dimensional trade-off between answer accuracy, parameter memory size, query latency, peak VRAM, and token consumption across methods?

audit_findings.claim_in_round2_report: P2 achieves 58.89 ms total latency (41.7% faster than B2 at 101.08 ms, 45.9% faster than B1 at 108.81 ms), peak VRAM of 357.14 MB, 20.28 MB checkpoint size, and cuts output tokens by 56.2% (Concise) to 81.2% (Minimal).

provenance_audit.hardware: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 Ti (4GB VRAM), torch.float16, CUDA

discrepancies_identified.latency_scope_conflation: The 58.89 ms (P2) vs 101.08 ms (B2) vs 108.81 ms (B1) latency figures in rq5_raw_results.json were measured for FIRST-TOKEN GENERATION (answer_tokens_generated = 1), reflecting prefill + single decode step. Full-response query latency in table 05_rq5_cost.csv is 4,249.31 ms (P2), 4,119.49 ms (B2), and 5,168.39 ms (B1). Round 2 reports failed to label 58.89 ms as first-token latency.
discrepancies_identified.token_reduction_provenance: The -56.2% and -81.2% output token savings in token_efficiency_scorecard.json were derived from analytical prompt budget formulas (14 vs 32 tokens, 6 vs 32 tokens) rather than empirical generation logs evaluated across a standardized test set with measured F1 retention.

audit_findings.valid_scientific_findings: Memory footprint and VRAM measurements are empirically grounded: SA-CMS memory module runs under 360 MB VRAM and 20.28 MB disk footprint on consumer 4GB hardware. Pre-fill attention latency is substantially lower when long document contexts are evicted from the prompt.
